editorial.headline: Technical Certification: A Nationally Open Practice, Including Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers certification across products, processes, services and systems, with foreign ownership open nationally and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
`71201` covers technical certification services: the independent assessment and certification of products, processes, services and management systems. Its scope reaches across the machinery of modern assurance, from quality, environmental, food-safety and energy-management systems to medical-device, supply-chain, laboratory-biorisk and anti-bribery management systems. It also includes certification connected with tourism, ecolabels, occupational safety and health, organic systems, sustainable forest management, timber legality, ISPO, halal products, green industry, construction services and warehouses.

The breadth matters because this is not confined to one commercial sector. The activity is defined by certification itself: work that examines whether a product, process, service or system meets the relevant basis for certification. The record also includes certification of business entities, independent assessors and verifiers, IndoGAP, organic food, forestry certification cooperation, Umrah and special Hajj organisers, and sustainable-event management systems. Taken together, it places technical certification at the point where operating practices, governance and sector-specific standards become matters capable of formal certification.

Registration is open at every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. Nationally, the activity is TERBUKA to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In practical terms, the record presents no national foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity. The stated PMA basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali does not reverse that national position. Its status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and it is not blocked for PMA registration by the provincial moratorium. The relevant Bali reason is specific: at the Besar scale, the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. That matters because the island-wide, permanent moratorium applies to Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. For this activity, the record therefore supports a clean conclusion: foreign investment is nationally open up to 100%, and Bali does not impose a moratorium block on its registration.
